topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture and establishes its learning objectives before the substantive discussion begins.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arising in susceptible cells can support cancer evolution within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how strongly environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk rather than cancer being an unavoidable consequence of chance.

topics.label: Infectious agents in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a detailed example of interacting infectious causes.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental exposures produce DNA damage through mechanisms shaped by the body's handling of those exposures.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and two-stage carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show why initiating mutations may require subsequent tumour-promoting conditions before cancer develops.

topics.label: Tissue susceptibility and synthesis of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics conclude the mechanistic account by explaining how the biological context of exposed cells shapes carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Human evidence linking carcinogen exposure to cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how evidence collected from people can connect particular exposures to cancer while acknowledging limits to causal inference.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how controlled biological tests reveal carcinogenic potential and why their results may not predict cancer in humans.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit reflection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by recapping its central conclusions and placing them within everyday risk–benefit decisions.
